verdict.rationale: LangGraph's durable execution model explicitly supports agents that 'persist through failures and can run for extended periods, automatically resuming from exactly where they left off,' backed by checkpointers/stores for state and a CLI/Agent Server for deployment — all core building blocks for autonomous background automations. However, evidence lacks any built-in scheduling/trigger mechanism (cron, webhooks, event triggers) to actually kick off runs autonomously, and community discussion raises open questions about production-grade deployment beyond local 'langgraph serve'. missing for 10: explicit scheduling/triggering support, independent hands-on confirmation of reliable long-running background execution in production.
